name: @w6w-apps/bexio
description: Manage contacts, invoices, quotes, orders, articles, projects and timesheets in bexio, the Swiss business/accounting/CRM platform.

w6w.longDescription:
bexio is a Swiss all-in-one business platform combining CRM, accounting, invoicing and project/time tracking for small and medium businesses. This app covers bexio's REST API v2 (`api.bexio.com`) end to end for the resources most workflows touch: contacts (create, edit, delete, search), sales documents (quotes, orders, invoices — including issuing an invoice), items/products (articles), projects and timesheets.

Every path, verb, query parameter, body field and enum here was verified on 2026-09-15 against bexio's own OpenAPI 3.0 document, extracted from the embedded Redoc state served at `docs.bexio.com` (bexio publishes no standalone `.json`/`.yaml` spec file), plus a live probe of the real Statuspage-hosted incident feed at `bexio-status.com`.

Two details in bexio's API are easy to get wrong from guesswork alone: every write — create AND edit — is a `POST` (there is no `PUT`/`PATCH` anywhere in the v2 surface, and edit reuses the exact same request schema as create), and every request must carry an explicit `Accept: application/json` header — the OpenAPI document marks it as a required parameter on every single operation, not just a conventional default. bexio also authenticates exclusively via OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect through a Keycloak realm at `auth.bexio.com` (there is no static API-key scheme for a third-party app); scopes are requested per resource and per direction (e.g. `contact_show` vs `contact_edit`), and requesting the write scope silently also grants the read scope for that resource.
